Due to the extremely low initial resistances (<0.1 W·cm2), relatively small changes resulted in a large percent increase in resistances of over 200% after 1,000 hours of outdoor aging. Nevertheless, the resistances fall well below the extrinsic resistances of solar devices (~1 W·cm2), and are comparable to the Aluzine-based TCCs (<0.2 W·cm2). Figure 22b shows the optical transmission spectrum before and after aging. Despite the aliphatic composition and the advertised properties of high-optical clarity and non- yellowing characteristics, a reduction in optical transparency near the UV region is observed. In comparison, a control sample demonstrated a near-coincident spectrum before and after 1,000 hours of storage in a desiccator. The large difference between the optical transparency of the TCC sample and the control is attributed to the nonuniform distribution of microspheres during TCC preparation. Unlike Aluzine epoxy, the Masterbond samples suffered from agglomeration of spheres and exacerbated the error between target concentration (i.e., 5% Ag-PMMA by area) and the actual microsphere coverage across samples and the area of interest. Due to time constraints, no further analysis was conducted for the Masterbond-based TCCs. Accelerated aging tests were conducted on encapsulated PSCs to quantify improvements in operational lifetimes compared to their unencapsulated counterparts. Task Summary: For PSC synthesis, indium tin oxide (ITO) coated glass substrates (ITO/Glass) were cleaned sequentially using Hellmanex (2% in deionized water), acetone, and isopropanol. Each step involved sonicating the substrates for 15 minutes. After drying with compressed air, substrates were further cleaned using UV-ozone for 15 minutes. MeO-2PACZ (0.5 mg/mL in ethanol) was spin-coated onto the ITO surface at 3,000 rpm for 30 s with an acceleration rate of 12,000 rpm s−1. The coated substrates were then annealed at 100 °C for 10 min.
